name: Political Science
notes: At least 15 courses (not counting prerequisites), minimum 2.0 GPA; at least 12 of 15 listed as INTR or PSCI; no S/F courses.
Prerequisites should be done by end of junior year. If CSC 161 or CSC 171 is used as a prerequisite, that same course may not also count anywhere in the body of the major.
MATH 165 requires a full calculus sequence first (14x users must take MATH 141-143).
At least one statistics or modeling tools course must be at the 3XX+ level - not auto-enforced.
Tools courses cannot double-count toward core track, breadth, or electives.
Transfer: none for tools/writing/team-learning; max two toward the core track; max three total; no online courses.
AP Government (4-5) or IB Global Politics HL (5-7) grants four credits, counted as elective + introductory + transfer.
Majors declared on/before April 15 2023 may count PSCI 282 as a modeling tools course.

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: two-semester calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Take two courses in one of the following calculus sequences: MATH 141-143 ...; MATH 161-162 ...; MATH 171-172

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: programming or linear algebra
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Take one of the following courses: CSC 161: Introduction to Programming; CSC 171: Introduction to Computer Science; MATH 165: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations

requirementGroups.label: Tools: argument
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must take PSCI 202W: Argument in Political Science.

requirementGroups.label: Tools: data analysis & statistics (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Take two of the following courses in data analysis and statistics: PSCI 200; PSCI 203W; PSCI 205; PSCI 404: Probability and Inference; PSCI 405: Causal Inference

requirementGroups.label: Tools: modeling (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Take two of the following courses in modeling: PSCI 107; PSCI 281; PSCI 288; PSCI 407: Mathematical Modeling; PSCI 408: Positive Political Theory

requirementGroups.label: Core track (5 courses from one field)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Core Track (Five Courses from One Track): Data and Modeling; Elections and Government; Philosophy, Law, and Public Policy; Political Economy and Development; Race, Ethnicity, and Identity; War, Violence, and Cooperation

requirementGroups.label: Breadth (2 courses outside your core track)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Select two track courses that are not in your core track.

requirementGroups.label: Electives (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Courses may be drawn from any offerings in the six tracks or any other courses in PSCI, INTR, ECON, HIST, or PHIL.

requirementGroups.label: Team learning (1+)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Select at least one team learning course. ... Options include research seminars, experiential learning, supervised teaching, independent study, directed research, senior honors project, and internships.
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the qualifying list is department-maintained; this filter is an approximation.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two W-designated courses in INTR or PSCI
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Select any two W-designated courses in INTR or PSCI. Included in the 15 courses listed above. No more than one of these courses may be used to satisfy the writing requirement in a second or third major.
